requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) performs source NAT translating node3's lan-a address to its own transit-facing address (192.168.20.1) as traffic enters the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS NAT source rule 10 (192.168.10.0/24 -> masquerade out eth1) was committed and confirmed via 'show nat source rules' (cmd-811a7262de954808). Conntrack directly shows src=192.168.10.12 (node3) translated to src=192.168.20.1 (node1) toward node4, both pre-restart (cmd-c8139a8bb79046da) and post-restart (cmd-5877c0d502374a73), confirming the translation is live and persistent.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) performs a second source NAT translating the transit-hop address to its own lan-b-facing address (192.168.30.1) as traffic enters lan-b
requirements.summary: OPNsense config.xml was edited to add opt1/opt2 interfaces and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule on opt2, applied via configctl. pfctl -s nat confirms 'nat on vtnet2 inet all -> (vtnet2:0)' is active (cmd-b917dfde42834869). pf state directly shows src 192.168.20.1 (node1) translated to 192.168.30.1 toward node4:8080, both pre-restart (cmd-e54ea63cbaaf4e63) and post-restart (cmd-3a7f90076a90487f).

requirements.requirement: node4 records the connection as arriving from node2 (192.168.30.1), not from node3 or node1
requirements.summary: node4's lanb-http.service journal log shows the client GET request logged with source IP 192.168.30.1 (node2's lan-b address) both before (cmd-603625c65c45454a) and after (cmd-a25d588faf05498e) the restart cycle, directly confirming the double-NAT hides node3/node1 addresses from node4.

requirements.requirement: End-to-end HTTP connectivity from node3 (lan-a) to node4:8080 (lan-b) works through the double-NAT path
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://192.168.30.13:8080/ returned HTTP 200 with the expected body, verified once before (cmd-218d755c26994764) and once after (cmd-22efb1b2319247fe) the full restart cycle.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart boot identity/baseline, a restart acknowledgement (or exec-stream-closed acknowledgement consistent with a reboot severing the session), polling until reconnection, a directly observed different post-restart boot identity, and recovered interfaces/NAT/routes/service state. Values are corroborated by the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot and executor_comparison diff (e.g. node1 boot_id 5bcff8f9→59c5eb4d, node2 kern.boottime 1781406916→1788670990 with a fresh 6s uptime, node3 boot_id d4784d1b→182d97ff, node4 boot_id 984a7d52→ca041523), and the double-NAT path was re-verified end-to-end after all four restarts.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the task -- VyOS SNAT to the transit address, OPNsense SNAT to the lan-b address, node4 observing only node2's address, and working end-to-end HTTP connectivity -- are directly evidenced via committed configuration plus live conntrack/pf-state and application-log observations, both before and after a full four-node restart cycle. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and directly corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots for all four nodes, with recovered NAT/interface/service state shown after each restart.
limitations: Restart acknowledgements for node3 and node4 returned 'exec stream closed before command completion' rather than a clean synchronous ack, which is expected behavior when a reboot severs the connection but means the ack itself is inferred rather than a captured success return code.

Physical NIC-to-peer topology was discovered empirically through many trial-and-error IP assignments and pings rather than being given, which somewhat obscures which specific commands were strictly necessary versus exploratory, though all were reverted before final configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: The bulk of the executor's mutating commands during physical-topology discovery (repeated ip addr add/flush, ifconfig alias add/delete on all four nodes to identify which NIC connects to which peer) were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted before final configuration, and were a reasonable prerequisite given the topology was not pre-labeled -- these are not penalized. One notable unnecessary mutation: cmd-8396dcdfe6fd43a3 disabled OPNsense's pf firewall entirely ('pfctl -d') as an ad hoc troubleshooting step to test whether pf was blocking a ping; this briefly weakened a security control on a managed node and had no causal role in the final solution, though it was reverted seconds later by cmd-25b6b16250594567 ('pfctl -e'). Minor low-risk residue remained after the task: an orphaned /tmp/www/index.html on node4 (superseded by /srv/www, cmd-cfb2fc53c4794d92) and evidence-collection artifacts (/tmp/out.txt, /tmp/reboot.log) on node3/node4, all low-risk and non-conflicting. No failed/conflicting services, no damaged package state, and NAT/firewall changes were the intended task outcome rather than residue.
